content.thinking:
Under the Act, the tenant must give at least two months' notice, so counting from 10 October the earliest possible end date would be 10 December 2026, regardless of the rent due date — unless the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date.

Rather than inventing details about keys or deposit timing, I should confirm the notice period to the tenant, ask the landlord for a decision on any shorter date, and note that deposit return happens via the standard check-out and inspection process through mydeposits once the tenancy ends.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job. Since the law changed on 1 May 2026, tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then. A shorter date is only possible if your landlord agrees to it in writing. We're asking him now and will let you know his answer by Friday 16 October. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you have that in writing. On keys and deposit: we'll confirm the key drop-off arrangements and a check-out appointment nearer the end date. Your deposit is held with mydeposits and is returned after check-out, once any deductions are agreed. We can't give an exact date yet. Thanks, Mare & Co Lettings

Do you agree to end the tenancy on 10 November 2026 (rent paid to that date)?
options: Keep to 10 December 2026 (the legal minimum). This is our default
Agree in writing to end on 10 November 2026
Agree to another date between 10 Nov and 10 Dec (please state it)

answers.question: Is the notice valid as given? What is the earliest end date under current law?
answers.answer: No: a tenant must give two months' written notice for an assured periodic tenancy. One month's notice does not end it on 10 Nov. Earliest end is 10 Dec 2026 (two months from 10 Oct).

answers.question: What options exist to end sooner?
answers.answer: Landlord agrees in writing to a shorter notice/earlier date (a surrender by agreement). The tenant has no right to leave earlier, and could be liable for rent to 10 Dec if the landlord doesn't agree. Re-letting sooner doesn't by itself end his liability without landlord agreement.

content.thinking:
Under the Act, the tenant must give at least two months' notice, so counting from 10 October the earliest possible end date would be 10 December 2026, regardless of the rent due date — unless the landlord agrees in writing to an earlier date.

Rather than inventing details about keys or deposit timing, I should confirm the notice period to the tenant, ask the landlord for a decision on any shorter date, and note that deposit return happens via the standard check-out and inspection process through mydeposits once the tenancy ends.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for letting us know, and good luck with the new job. Since the law changed on 1 May 2026, tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. Counting from your email today (10 October), the earliest your tenancy can end is 10 December 2026. Your rent stays payable until then. A shorter date is only possible if your landlord agrees to it in writing. We're asking him now and will let you know his answer by Friday 16 October. Please don't treat 10 November as agreed until you have that in writing. On keys and deposit: we'll confirm the key drop-off arrangements and a check-out appointment nearer the end date. Your deposit is held with mydeposits and is returned after check-out, once any deductions are agreed. We can't give an exact date yet. Thanks, Mare & Co Lettings

Do you agree to end the tenancy on 10 November 2026 (rent paid to that date)?
options: Keep to 10 December 2026 (the legal minimum). This is our default
Agree in writing to end on 10 November 2026
Agree to another date between 10 Nov and 10 Dec (please state it)
